newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber in selling ahead of Thai meeting.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber in selling ahead of Thai meeting.

text.p: Singapore rubber market players unloaded their holdings in a wave of profit-taking at the close on Monday ahead of a Thai cabinet meeting tomorrow which may yield further news on a rubber deal with China, dealers said.
The sharp fall of the dollar against the yen also saw some players engaging in arbitrage between the Japanese and Singapore rubber markets, they added.

"People wanted to clear their positions ahead of the Thai cabinet meeting tomorrow. They wanted to cash in their profits before then because they are wary the cabinet may come up with another announcement," a trader said.

Bangkok recently announced it was raising its intervention price for RSS3 grade rubber to 29 baht a kg from 27.50 baht. Traders said they were also watching talks between Thai and Chinese officials on a rubber deal under which Beijing will buy 382,000 tonnes of rubber for 1997.
"Some players are also doing some arbitrage between the Tokyo and Singapore (rubber) markets," another dealer said.
At 0945 GMT, July RSS3 was seen at 110.00 U.S. cents a kg from 108.50 cents. July RSS1 was seen at 159.50 Singapore cents (US$1.11) a kg from 157.50 cents.
